 Experts' Takeaways Lions Dominate Pats Vikings Crush Packers What I'm Hearing Analysis 49ers erupt for 584 yards to outlast Cowboys: What can’t Brock Purdy do?
 Brock Purdy and Christian McCaffrey led an explosive offensive performance as the 49ers piled up a season-high in points and total offense against the Cowboys. Stacy Revere / Getty Images 
 By Jon Machota , Vic Tafur and David DeChant Nov. 15, 2026 Updated 8:37 pm EST Share article 75 ARLINGTON, Texas — Brock Purdy showed off his arm, legs and even his blocking ability as the San Francisco 49ers racked up 584 total yards and outscored the Dallas Cowboys for a 46-40 win on Sunday at AT&T Stadium. 
 The 584 yards were the most by the 49ers since 2012 and fifth-most in franchise history. 
 Advertisement
 Starting late in the second quarter with a 74-yard pass from a scrambling Purdy to Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco scored touchdowns on four of five possessions to take a 38-19 lead with 11:26 left in the game. After Kaelon Black bulldozed for a 25-yard touchdown run, Deebo Samuel broke a 70-yard TD run on a reverse, with Purdy throwing blocks more than 25 yards downfield. McCaffrey added a 16-yard touchdown to cap the surge.
 Dallas closed within 38-32 with 3:23 to play, but Purdy hit McCaffrey for a 66-yard touchdown (and a 2-point conversion) two plays later to reclaim a 14-point lead.
 Purdy finished 22-of-28 passing for 389 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions despite being under frequent pressure, taking five sacks and being hit two additional times. McCaffrey finished with 223 total yards and three touchdowns, as the 49ers pushed their league-best record to 8-1. 
 The Cowboys lost their fifth straight meeting with the Niners and fell to 4-6 despite getting 11 catches for 145 yards and three touchdowns from George Pickens, who returned from a one-game injury absence. Dallas has not beaten a team with a winning record or won consecutive games since November 2025. 
 Top Plays from 49ers @ Cowboys Box score | Week 10 live blog | Game discussion 
 What can’t Purdy do? 
 What if, like a boxing champion, Purdy gets even better after he gets knocked down? Purdy was sacked five times but still did whatever he wanted Sunday. In fact, he was toying with the Cowboys’ defense at times. 
 With the 49ers trailing 17-16 in the second quarter, Purdy started to take off on a run, stopped on a dime and hit McCaffrey in stride on a short pass. McCaffrey took it 74 yards for a touchdown. Purdy also threw a touchdown pass to Samuel, and later, on a Samuel reverse, sprinted downfield looking for someone to block. Or at least stand in the way of, as Samuel went all the way 70 yards for the score. 
 Advertisement
 Then, Purdy ran twice for 21 yards. On the first, he stopped and pump-faked a pass as the traumatized Cowboys froze, then continued running for the first down. Later, Purdy faked an option pitch to … no one … as he turned the corner for 9 yards.  
 The Vikings defense looms large as the 49ers’ next opponent, but Minnesota has to be concerned about everything Purdy does, too. — Vic Tafur, 49ers beat writer   
 The 49ers’ RBs dominated, especially after halftime 
 A 49ers running game that was bottled up in the first half popped in the second with help from Black. The rookie scored on a punishing, tackle-breaking 25-yard touchdown run on the team’s opening drive in the third quarter. He also had a huge block in pass protection against Cowboys defensive tackle Quinnen Williams, who’d been a 49ers scourge in the first half. Williams was knocked off his feet and had to come out of the game for two snaps. On the second of those snaps, Black took a carry to the right, handed it to Samuel as he ran in the other direction, then watched as Samuel cruised 70 yards for the touchdown. 
 While Black rumbled on the ground, McCaffrey scored two long catch-and-run touchdowns and added his own 16-yard touchdown early in the fourth quarter. Black finished with 53 rushing yards, and McCaffrey had 62. The 49ers, who rushed for 45 yards in the first half, finished with 214 . — Matt Barrows, 49ers beat writer 
 Keenan Allen stands out in 49ers debut 
 Allen looked like someone who’s been working with Purdy for the past five years, not the past five days. The veteran receiver, who practiced with his new team for the first time Wednesday, was Purdy’s top target in the first half and ended up catching five of seven targets for 61 yards. Allen was on the field for 23 offensive snaps, an impressive amount for a newcomer. 
 Advertisement
 The 49ers played their third straight game without top receiver Mike Evans, who’s coming back from Achilles tendinitis. Coach Kyle Shanahan has said there’s “a chance” Evans could play in next week’s showdown with the Vikings in Mexico City. Samuel returned from a hamstring injury Sunday, scoring two touchdowns, while Jordan Watkins continued his ascent in finishing with two big catches for 49 yards. 
 With Allen in the lineup, Brandin Cooks was a healthy scratch. It’s unknown who the odd man out will be when Evans returns, although Jacob Cowing nearly had a calamitous punt return Sunday — he slipped as the ball arrived — and was not targeted in the passing game. — Barrows 
 Why does the Cowboys’ defense continue to struggle with open-field pursuit/tackling? 
 For starters, they’re just not a good defense. The fundamentals have been an issue all season. If it’s not an outside linebacker failing to keep contain, it’s a linebacker or defensive back failing to wrap up. Just recently, we’ve seen this with Arizona’s Tyler Allgeier busting off runs of 63 and 52 yards. Then it was Indianapolis’ Ashton Dulin for 55 yards last week. So, San Francisco doing the same is no surprise. The 49ers are a far superior team. You expect Samuel and McCaffrey to do the same, which they did. 
 It’s easy to blame first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker, but the Cowboys had similar issues with a different coaching staff and a largely different roster. That’s why these issues fall just as much on the front office and head coach. — Jon Machota, Cowboys beat writer 
 What does this game mean for the Cowboys’ big picture? 
 At this point, it really doesn’t matter if the Cowboys stay in the NFC East race. They’re not beating any quality opponents with this defense. They’ll probably stay in that divisional race, though, because the entire group is awful. Looking at the rest of the schedule, the Cowboys have a realistic shot to beat the Titans, Eagles, Giants and Commanders. It seems highly unlikely that they’ll beat the Seahawks, Rams or Jaguars. That leaves Dallas around 8-9 to finish the season. The Giants have a more difficult schedule, so it’s possible to catch them. But why would anyone want to see these teams play any NFC North squad in a playoff game? — Machota
